target: Claude Code v2.1.246, installed native ARM64 executable
configuration: Safe mode; no tools; empty strict MCP configuration; no generative prompts submitted

captures.scope: Slash picker, arrow selection, Tab acceptance, shortcut help, multiline input, Ctrl+C
Filtered help, Escape dismissal, Ctrl+S stash and restore, double Escape

observations.behavior: Prompt sits between horizontal rules near the bottom of the terminal, with a compact shortcut footer.
Slash opens a command list with descriptions. Down changes the selected command, and Tab inserts that command with an argument hint.
Question mark on an empty prompt expands inline shortcuts. Escape closes them.
Alt+Enter followed by typing produces a second input line. Ctrl+C clears the draft.
Typing /he filters suggestions. Enter opens help, and Escape returns to an empty prompt.
Ctrl+S stashes a draft with a footer indicator, and Ctrl+S on the empty prompt restores it.
First Escape shows a clear hint; a second Escape clears the draft.

documented_adaptations.behavior: Ctrl+R opens history search; Enter or Tab restores a selection for editing.
Shift+Enter and backslash+Enter are alternate newline shortcuts.

portfolio_decisions: Keep the cyan pixel bat, welcome box, product order, and portfolio content.
Use the observed picker and editing interactions for allowlisted browser-local commands.
Keep history and stashed drafts in memory, limited to this tab.
Provide touch controls, visible focus, concise status announcements, and normal readable page scrolling.
Keep all commands within portfolio exploration; no shell or AI backend is introduced.
limits: Study covers this installed version and the selected safe-mode configuration, not all Claude Code versions or customizations.
No inspection of existing Claude prompt history or model/tool execution was performed.
Raw captures stay outside the published Site; this ledger contains only the relevant observations.
REA process sampling can omit short-lived descendants and does not observe network activity or all filesystem effects.
Terminal pixel equivalence and proprietary implementation recovery were not claimed.
